description.narrative: This event is a pilot initiative organized by the United Nations (UN) Women aimed at enhancing the employability of over 150 female STEM graduates (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) and accelerating the inclusion of young women in the STEM sector in Tunisia. The event brings together key stakeholders, including business leaders, policymakers, civil society, financial institutions, UN Women, and the academic community, in a national gathering.The event follows a multi-stakeholder learning approach, engaging partners from the public sector, private sector, and civil society. It addresses key issues such as gender equality (SDG 5) and decent work and economic growth (SDG 8), with a particular focus on the inclusion of young women. By focusing on STEM, it provides young people with access to quality jobs that offer sustainable, decent working conditions and stable income. The job fair is a results-driven intervention designed to accelerate gender equality in STEM by empowering young women with skills, networks, and opportunities for success in the labor market. This approach combines structural change with direct impact and integrates high-level policy dialogue with business engagement.Through targeted career acceleration sessions and strategic connections with leading STEM employers, WYSE (Women & Youth Employment in STEM sector Event) aims to improve the employability of over 150 female STEM graduates. The event also encourages institutions to commit to gender-sensitive recruitment practices. It aims to bridging the gap between qualified women and STEM roles, promoting inclusive policies, and setting a new standard for sustainable transformation in Tunisia's labor market.
